code_improvements.title: Add Canvas State Snapshot Persistence
code_improvements.description: Create a useCanvasSnapshots hook that extends the existing HistoryContext to support named snapshots with persistence across sessions. Users can save, name, and restore specific canvas states. Builds on the usePromptHistory pattern for CRUD operations with favorites and search.
code_improvements.rationale: The usePromptHistory hook (src/hooks/usePromptHistory.ts) already establishes the pattern: PromptRecord interface, StorageManager backing, favorites, timestamps, search. The HistoryContext exists for in-session undo/redo but lacks persistence. Combining these patterns enables a complete design versioning system.
existing_patterns: usePromptHistory: PromptRecord with id, isFavorite, useCount, timestamps
code_improvements.implementation_approach: 1. Add canvasSnapshotsStorage instance to storageManager.ts. 2. Create SnapshotRecord interface following PromptRecord: id, name, thumbnail, canvasState (JSON), isFavorite, createdAt. 3. Create useCanvasSnapshots hook with addSnapshot, restoreSnapshot, renameSnapshot, deleteSnapshot, toggleFavorite, searchSnapshots. 4. Integrate with CanvasEditor for save/restore buttons.

code_improvements.title: Extend Canvas Commands with Batch Element Operations
code_improvements.description: Add BatchDeleteElements, BatchUpdateElements, and BatchMoveElements commands following the established batch command pattern from imageCommands.ts. Enables bulk operations on multiple canvas elements via voice or UI.
code_improvements.rationale: BatchUpscaleCommand and BatchRemoveBackgroundCommand in imageCommands.ts demonstrate the batch pattern: iterate over items, collect results/errors, handle partial failures gracefully. Canvas commands only have single-element operations. The Command interface and ToolSchemas registry support this extension.
existing_patterns: BatchUpscaleCommand: for-loop with try-catch per item, results[] and errors[] collection
DeleteElementCommand.execute: single element deletion with context.canvasCallbacks
code_improvements.implementation_approach: 1. Add BatchDeleteElementsSchema, BatchUpdateElementsSchema to validationSchemas.ts: z.object({ element_ids: z.array(z.string()) }). 2. Create BatchDeleteElementsCommand following BatchUpscaleCommand structure. 3. Create BatchUpdateElementsCommand for bulk property changes. 4. Register in ToolSchemas and ensure actionExecutor routes correctly.

code_improvements.title: Add Error Recovery Suggestions Hook
code_improvements.description: Create a useErrorRecovery hook that provides actionable recovery suggestions based on the existing error classification system. Maps error types (network, cors, timeout, api, etc.) to specific user actions (retry, check API key, wait for rate limit).
code_improvements.rationale: The errorHandler.ts already classifies errors into structured NetworkError types with retryable flags and dispatches 'error-tracked' CustomEvents. The withRetry function handles automatic retries. This infrastructure enables a user-facing recovery suggestion system without new error handling logic.
existing_patterns: classifyError: returns { type: 'network'|'cors'|'timeout'|'api', retryable: boolean, message: string }
useErrorMetrics: listens to events, aggregates metrics
code_improvements.implementation_approach: 1. Create RECOVERY_SUGGESTIONS map: { network: 'Check internet connection', api: 'Verify API key in Settings', timeout: 'Try again - server was slow', cors: 'This operation not supported' }. 2. Create useErrorRecovery hook listening to 'error-tracked' events. 3. Return { lastError, suggestions, canRetry, retryAction }. 4. Integrate with Toast for actionable error messages.

code_improvements.title: Add Layout Expert Agent to Registry
code_improvements.description: Add a 'Layout Expert' specialized agent to AGENT_REGISTRY for banner composition, element positioning, safe zones, and visual hierarchy. Uses the existing AgentDefinition interface with appropriate keywords for automatic routing.
code_improvements.rationale: The agentRegistry.ts has 4 well-established agents (Benno, Art Director, Copy Specialist, Tech Wizard) following AgentDefinition interface. The getAgentSuggestions function handles new agents automatically via keyword matching - no routing changes needed. Layout/positioning expertise is missing from current agents.
existing_patterns: AgentDefinition: { id, name, description, capabilities, systemPrompt, keywords, icon }
Art Director agent structure: keywords array, capabilities array
Keyword scoring in getAgentSuggestions: score += 0.3 per keyword match
code_improvements.implementation_approach: 1. Add new AgentDefinition object to AGENT_REGISTRY. 2. Set id: 'layout-expert', name: 'Layout Expert'. 3. Keywords: ['layout', 'position', 'center', 'align', 'space', 'safe zone', 'composition', 'hierarchy', 'arrange', 'grid']. 4. Capabilities: ['list_elements', 'update_element', 'analyze_banner']. 5. SystemPrompt focused on LinkedIn safe zones, visual hierarchy, element spacing.

code_improvements.title: Add Model Performance Comparison Utility
code_improvements.description: Create a compareModelPerformance utility that combines MODEL_METADATA_REGISTRY theoretical scores with useModelMetrics actual usage data to rank and recommend models. Enables data-driven model selection that improves with usage.
code_improvements.rationale: MODEL_METADATA_REGISTRY (modelRouter.ts) has qualityScore, avgResponseTime, costPerCall for each model. useModelMetrics aggregates actual stats.byModel with calls, avgTime, successRate. These exist independently - combining them enables intelligent recommendations based on real performance.
existing_patterns: stats.byModel[modelId]: { calls, avgTime, successRate, errors, totalCost }
getModelMetadataById: memoized lookup for model metadata
code_improvements.implementation_approach: 1. Add getModelRecommendations(operation: OperationType) to modelRouter.ts. 2. Fetch theoretical scores from REGISTRY and actual stats from modelMetricsStorage. 3. Compute weighted score: 40% actual successRate (if data exists), 30% response time, 20% qualityScore, 10% cost efficiency. 4. Return sorted array of { modelId, score, hasUsageData }. 5. Optionally show 'Recommended' badge in ModelSelector based on this ranking.
